description:
About: Tech enthusiast into space data, coding, and building fast prototypes.

Looking for: Teammates with good vibes, late-night stamina, and skills in dev, design, or research. Just here to hack with friends, build something cool, and survive on coffee! 🚀
summary: Orbvitals is a visual, offline health self-assessment tool for astronauts on long-duration missions. In a 2-minute daily check-in, the astronaut logs nine health indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, glucose, temperature, sleep, mood, exercise and radiation dose). Orbvitals turns them into a clickable body map with green / amber / red status, plain-language explanations and concrete actions. It addresses the challenge by letting astronauts evaluate and act on their own health. It matters because, far from Earth, medical help is delayed: Orbvitals compares each astronaut with their own baseline, detects multi-indicator patterns, and switches to an autonomous onboard protocol when the communication delay to Earth is too long.
details:
What it does

  • Daily check-in with sliders and "how to measure" instructions for each indicator; the body map changes color live while values move.
  • Body map with seven zones (brain & behavior, heart & circulation, lungs, metabolism, immune system, bones & muscles, radiation). Tapping a zone explains its function, how spaceflight affects it, today's value vs. the astronaut's normal, what to do, and the related NASA hazard.
  • Personal baseline: the first 14 days define each astronaut's normal range; values that drift in a harmful direction are flagged even if they are still within general ranges.
  • Pattern detection across indicators: behavioral strain (sleep, mood and exercise dropping together), possible infection (temperature plus heart rate), cardiovascular deconditioning (low exercise plus rising resting heart rate) and solar particle events.
  • Mission view: a schematic Earth–Mars Hohmann transfer (solved with Kepler's equation) gives the ship-to-Earth distance and light-time delay. Delay sets the medical support mode: real-time (< 5 s), delayed (5 s to 5 min) or autonomous (> 5 min). Also covers ISS and lunar profiles, the daily radiation environment, cumulative mission dose vs. NASA's 600 mSv career limit, and a solar-storm simulation with a shelter protocol.
  • Report to Earth: the astronaut chooses to send a summary, which travels with real light-time; a flight surgeon console shows the received reports for each crew member.
  • Trends (30 days against the personal baseline band), routine adherence and streaks, an in-app guide, and an English / Spanish toggle.

Benefits

  • Earlier detection of personal changes, clear guidance for non-experts, autonomy when Earth cannot answer in time, and privacy: data stays on the device unless the astronaut sends it.

Goals

  • Help crews prevent critical conditions on long missions, and in the future serve remote workers on Earth (Antarctic stations, offshore crews, rural clinics).

Tools and technology

  • Single-file web app in HTML, CSS and JavaScript (inline SVG for the body and orbit map, custom charts), no backend, works offline. Deployed on Vercel. Demo data is simulated with fixed seeds; health ranges are illustrative and the app is not a medical device.
